name: Chest and shoulder stretch
pattern: Static hold: the arm is held out, across, overhead or behind you to lengthen the chest, shoulder, lats or upper arm.
setup: Stand in a doorway or beside a wall corner.
Raise one arm to the side, elbow bent 90° at shoulder height, forearm on the frame.
Feet split, chest tall, shoulder blades gently back and down.

steps.text: Step through with the near foot and turn the chest slightly away until the front of the shoulder pulls.
Stay still 15-30 s. Keep the shoulder down, ribs down.
Come out slowly, then switch sides.

cues.cue: One arm on the frame, elbow at or a bit below shoulder height.
cues.why: The one-arm doorway stretch lengthened the pec minor more than two lying or seated stretches.

cues.cue: Shoulder blades back and down before you lean.
cues.why: It puts the stretch on the chest instead of the front of the shoulder joint.

cues.cue: For the back of the shoulder, pull the arm across the chest, shoulder blade still.
cues.why: The cross-body stretch (5 x 30 s daily) improved shoulder internal rotation by about 20° in 4 weeks.

cues.cue: Overhead and behind-the-back: ribs down, low back neutral.
cues.why: Arching fakes range from the spine.

cues.cue: Ease in to a mild pull, never pain.
cues.why: Gentle stretches still gain range; stretching into pain did not help and can irritate the muscle.

cues.cue: Hold 15-30 s, 2-4 times, about 60 s in total per side.
cues.why: 30 s holds gave the same gains as 60 s; aim for at least 5 min per muscle each week, most days.

breathing: Breathe slowly and normally. Ease a little deeper as you breathe out.

tempo.note: Ease in for about 3 s, hold 15-30 s, ease out. Repeat 2-4 times each side.

mistakes.name: Shoulder hikes up
mistakes.looks: The shoulder creeps toward the ear as you lean or pull.
mistakes.fix: Shoulder down and back, then go less deep.
mistakes.why: The upper trap takes over and the target muscle stays slack.

mistakes.name: Low back arches
mistakes.looks: Ribs flare and the low back sways, especially overhead.
mistakes.why: The spine bends instead of the shoulder.

mistakes.name: Arm too high on the frame
mistakes.looks: The elbow is far above the shoulder and the front of the shoulder pinches.
mistakes.fix: Lower the elbow to shoulder height or just below.
mistakes.why: Pinching at the front of the joint, not a muscle stretch.

mistakes.name: Bouncing
mistakes.looks: You bob in and out of the stretch instead of holding still.
mistakes.fix: Ease in slowly, then stay still and let it relax.
mistakes.why: Bouncing triggers the muscle to tighten back and can strain it.

safety: Shoulder that has dislocated: avoid arm out and turned back (doorway, behind-the-back) unless cleared.
Pins and needles in the hand: lower the arm, a nerve is tensioned.
Pinch at the front or top of the shoulder: change the angle; do not push through.

variants.change: Both arms in a corner: same position, stretches both sides; keep the head from poking forward.
Hold a towel, band or stick to reach behind or overhead when hands cannot meet.
Contract-relax: push gently against the stretch for 3-6 s, relax, then ease deeper. Similar range gains to static holds; also best after training.
A partner moves the limb. Go slowly and say when you feel a mild pull; the partner holds there, never pushes into pain.
Moving version: controlled swings through the range, 8-12 reps. Better before training than long holds.

harder: overhead lat stretch on a bench

subtypes.name: Sleeper stretch
subtypes.change: Lie on your side on the arm to be stretched, arm in front at 90°, elbow bent; ease the forearm down.

subtypes.name: Overhead triceps stretch
subtypes.change: Reach one arm up, bend the elbow so the hand drops behind the head; other hand eases the elbow back.

subtypes.name: Cross-body shoulder stretch
subtypes.match: cross over|across|cross body|wrap around|crossover|rear deltoid|bent arm shoulder|one arm cross
subtypes.change: Bring one arm across the chest at shoulder height; other forearm pulls it closer. Shoulder blade still.

subtypes.name: Dead hang
subtypes.change: Hang from a bar, arms straight, feet down or on the floor; let the shoulders rise gently.

subtypes.name: Hands-behind-head chest stretch
subtypes.change: Hands behind the head, elbows wide; draw the elbows back.

subtypes.name: Behind-the-back stretch
subtypes.match: behind the back|behind back|hands behind|clasp|towel|biceps|reverse|backward|shoulder flexor|upright shoulders|straight arms|chest out|elbow flexor|preacher|on a support|in vertical|squeeze shoulder blades
subtypes.change: Hands clasped or holding a towel behind you, arms straight; lift them slightly and open the chest.

subtypes.name: Overhead lat stretch
subtypes.change: Kneel and reach the arms forward onto a bench, ball or the floor; sink the chest down.

subtypes.name: Lying or partner chest stretch
subtypes.change: Lie face up with arms out to the sides, or let a partner draw the arms back slowly.

metrics.label: Movement during hold
metrics.good: < 3° once you are in the stretch

motion.basis: Doorway stretch from borstad2006 (pec minor), cross-body dose from mcclure2007. Horizontal movement has no joint key: shoulderAbd -40 at 90° flexion stands for across the body, shoulderFlex -15 at 90° abduction for arm drawn back. Other angles estimated.
